title: The diagonal was already there
description: Eight source vertices become the cube; moving corner 6 reveals the unchanged front diagonal.
limitation: Actual builder vertices, triangle indices and mesh update function. Construction timing and materials are staged.

title: One rule makes a family
description: One angular rule makes two straight columns. A fixed four-sided, two-metre reference stands beside editable height and radial count; the two-ring position list stays visible in the geometry.
limitation: Port of the Function browser study, not the museum's richer profile generator. Height 1–3 m in 0.1 m steps; radial counts 4, 6, 8, 12, 16. A declared 0.70 m display radius replaces browser pixels. Side faces and top cap only. Rendering duplicates corners for flat normals; the input list contains exactly 2*n positions.

title: A value places a body
description: A native sphere responds to the browser study's height value; an optional mistaken one-metre offset separates its displayed and expected positions. Four physical controls lower, raise, toggle the offset and reset.
limitation: A faithful port of drawPoint, with height 0–3 m in 0.1 m steps and default1.2 m. A visible representation of a point, not a controller for the existing museum coordinate artifact. The +1 m is an incorrect value sent to a local receiver.

title: Read a candidate. Keep a position. Join a pair.
description: Eight given positions become a retained list by the exact distance >=0.8 m test. The learner reads candidates and separately joins retained neighbours, with both route and stored list visible in 3D.
limitation: Fixed candidates from the browser study, not live hand tracking or a replay of a museum drawing. Two-dimensional source positions are embedded on a 3D table with equal units; joining does not alter those positions.

title: A profile travels
description: Two O profiles and one I become a passage, an open vessel and a closed sweep. Sections expose the operation before their boundary edges become surfaces.
limitation: Construction timing is staged. Final vertices come from the unchanged gallery recipes. The O keeps its sill and the vessel remains open at both ends.

title: A passage follows a body
description: The wall opens near an approaching body and moves its gap as the body walks along it.
limitation: Actual per-slat targets, clearance rule and hinge transforms on a private copy. Shows target poses rather than live easing and visitor detection.

title: A lift, then a slide
description: A panel follows the source's lift-then-slide route; another takes one diagonal to the same corner.
limitation: Paths and dimensions come from the original door. This is a chosen diagonal in the free mode, not a claim that free motion has only one route.

title: A response can remember
description: A teaching clock moves a cube while two physical gate models compare present proximity with a retained visit. FRAME, APPROACH / AWAY and RESET let the visitor separate the events.
limitation: Exact State browser-study transitions presented in 3D. Each FRAME adds a synthetic 0.5 seconds; it is not a measured engine frame. APPROACH is an explicit input, not player tracking. No museum gate is controlled.

title: Only the children grow
description: The small exit grows with its parent room; the separate reference doorway keeps its size.
limitation: Uses actual door-wall construction, witness placement and factor four; omits furniture, player relocation and collision demonstration. Whole exhibit reduced to 26% scale.

title: The same operations, another order
description: Rotation and translation unfold in both orders, then the results share one origin.
limitation: Actual workbench transformations and tetrahedron; interpolation is explanatory staging.

title: An address keeps a place
description: Rows become a volume of fixed addresses; their nested frames rotate, move and scale.
limitation: Replays existing seeded Molnar poses, not live hand interaction.

title: One phase travels through sixty-four addresses
description: A snake advances along addressed cells, wraps through zero and changes palette without changing its rule.
limitation: Original 8 by 8 snake value function and palettes. Raised active cells are a reading aid; the live disco floor changes colour.

title: An empty address still exists
description: Sixteen persistent sockets distinguish selecting an address, toggling its Boolean and overwriting the grid with a checker rule.
limitation: A native port of the browser teaching study; its private cells do not control the museum floor. Height displays occupancy, not a third array index.

title: A turn crosses the floor
description: A physical four-by-four sample changes one tile at a time, followed by the full field and an eye chart.
limitation: Actual rule images on explanatory 3D tile slabs; no new tiling algorithm.

title: Where does the column end?
description: A column rises from dark to light; its matching ceiling arrives and its edge becomes difficult to see.
limitation: Shared source HSV function and shader on simplified cylinders; apparent fog is colour matching.

title: One class; whose state changes?
description: Two colour receivers read actual RefCounted Palette objects. Separate reference paths converge when both receivers share one instance.
limitation: Proposed Palette teaching class, with the browser's three inks and reset semantics; no claim that existing museum floor cells already use this class. Receivers refresh explicitly.

title: The space changes the colours between
description: Source RGB and HSV interpolation take different routes between red and cyan, plotted inside one three-dimensional RGB cube.
limitation: Uses all 16 original samples. Plot positions are an explanatory RGB embedding; both routes use the same colour-space axes.

title: How many colours fit the same arch?
description: Two, six, seven and forty-eight authored bands divide the same width; separated layers join into each arc.
limitation: Original planar band meshes and authored palettes, reduced to 15% scale. Depth separation stages the construction; no optical rainbow simulation.

title: A fragment becomes a pattern
description: A source motif unfolds through p4m symmetry; editing one cell changes its distant occurrences.
limitation: Actual source colour lookup raised into a 3D relief; the original mill generates a texture.

title: One hill, different slopes
description: Two perpendicular sections pass through one point of the terrain, revealing opposite signed partial slopes.
limitation: Samples the existing analytic height and derivative functions; explanatory marker and section overlays.

title: The next position is another lookup
description: Three source particles repeatedly sample one held direction field and retain their different trajectories.
limitation: A fixed seed and three declared starts; 160 source steps of 0.05 seconds. Directions, not forces. The chosen trajectories do not wrap.

title: A force changes a journey
description: Two source force vectors meet head to tail; their sum bends a journey, then equal opposing forces leave prior motion intact.
limitation: Actual source vectors. The motion interval is ideal unit mass without source contacts or damping.

title: A longer arm, a smaller push
description: Actual crank geometry exposes parallel and perpendicular push components, then compares three arm/push purchases.
limitation: Static source poses, not angular dynamics. Rigs are enlarged for inspection; the three purchase alternatives keep a common display scale.

title: A waist and sixteen intervals
description: Boundary rings, the narrow waist and sampled sections reveal how the actual catenoid surface is assembled.
limitation: Analytic catenoid with c=0.82, height range -1 to 1, 16 by 48 intervals. No settling, stability test or universal area-minimum claim.

title: A network settles into a body
description: A 4-by-3-by-4 lattice gains springs and settles through the bench solver, retaining a ghost of the starting shape.
limitation: Fixed-seed replay of source initialization; the museum bench normally displays only its settled snapshot.

title: A turn leaves its coordinates
description: Original rotating-point and bridge functions show sine projection, then retain cosine in depth with the source helix option.
limitation: One 81-sample cycle. Small non-colliding bridge specimens; interpolating between sine and helix is explanatory staging.

title: A movement reaches its neighbours
description: A centre pulse reaches neighbouring oscillators; a second lattice with zero coupling receives the same pulse.
limitation: Existing fixed-step oscillator solver; private start-state copies, slowed for inspection.

title: A choice becomes a passage
description: One seeded diagonal decision per cell becomes a four-by-four arrangement of walls.
limitation: One fixed seed and 16 cells; not every gap is connected.

title: A number has a previous state
description: The original crank arithmetic fills a 64-bit block register, masks to 32 bits and replays sixteen outputs from the same seed.
limitation: Blocks represent integer bit places, not circuitry. Sixteen matching outputs establish this replay, not distribution quality or cryptographic security.

title: Three fields, one height
description: Separate authored noise layers meet at the same addresses, then sum and undergo the source's slope pass.
limitation: A 25-by-25 display sampling over the 200 m source span; display scales are explicit, not a full terrain simulation.

title: One sample becomes colour and distance
description: The actual study sampler and radius function turn one field into skin and relief, then compare direct and warped addresses.
limitation: A 48-segment, 24-ring display sphere uses the existing CPU study, not the older animated dome shader. Skin-to-relief interpolation is staged; source endpoint values and seeds are retained.

title: One function, many addresses
description: An unchanged sphere mesh receives the original UV tile shader; grid frequency changes while its faces stay fixed.
limitation: The original flat-display shader is transferred to spheres, exposing their UV distortion. TIME is replaced by a private film clock; animate stays zero.

title: A surface answers a view
description: Orbit a fixed torus while the source oil-slick shader answers the changing normal/view angle.
limitation: Source optical approximation, not physical thin-film simulation; only TIME is replaced by the film clock.

title: Three neighbours choose one next cell
description: The actual elementary rule selects an output from three input bits, then repeats around wrapped rows.
limitation: Height separates recorded generations; no added spatial cellular-automaton dimension.

title: A generation becomes a storey
description: A three-neighbour birth is revealed, then actual Life states stack vertically as retained time.
limitation: A declared eight-by-eight wrapped glider fixture; later walker erosion is excluded.

title: Keep two thirds; repeat the cut
description: The actual Cantor recursion supplies retained bars while removed thirds move aside.
limitation: Five finite removals; staging of cut material does not establish an infinite-set claim.

title: Twenty of twenty-seven
description: Separate 27 cells, remove the source's seven omitted positions, and repeat the retained-index rule.
limitation: Two finite subdivision depths, not an infinite sponge.

title: Forward is a local direction
description: Follow the actual 3D Hilbert turtle segments through two rewrites and around a spatial orbit.
limitation: Finite generations; marker points along the current segment, rather than claiming to expose an unrecorded full turtle frame.

title: Which requests make the next branch?
description: Show real target assignments, unit directions, their normalized sum, and the resulting network growth.
limitation: One authored asymmetric field with NETWORK policy and a finite node/iteration budget.

title: A sheet is held by relations
description: Reveal the actual membrane's pins and distance constraints while replaying a computed grip and release.
limitation: Educational membrane, not measured fabric; six seconds of actual fixed-step solver output slowed for inspection.

title: A yielding body begins with a skin
description: The actual BoxMesh separates into face data, indexed triangles and its source-selected crown pin.
limitation: Shows rest geometry and attachment, not a substitute simulation of inflation or deformation.

title: A surface between eight samples
description: Eight corner samples become crossings and lookup triangles; margin moves the sheet while classification stays fixed.
limitation: One cell, using the source extractor; no claim that this one demonstration resolves ambiguous marching-cubes cases.

title: Two contributions become one boundary
description: The original field generator adds two inverse-square sources and extracts a shared threshold as their centres approach.
limitation: Reduced fixed sampling lattice and 21 cached surfaces; no changes to the live museum generator.

title: Only what both solids contain
description: Native CSG computes the source box-sphere intersections at all four named offsets.
limitation: Geometric intersection does not prove the source comments’ social analogies.

title: A walk taken out of a block
description: Follow the eleven original seeded cutter centres, their union, and the subtraction from a sectioned block.
limitation: A cutter union is not clipped to the stock; cutter connectivity does not establish body clearance.

title: One body, several neighbours
description: Freeze one body, inspect its neighbourhood and three steering contributions, then run the original updater on a private flock.
limitation: A bounded eight-body teaching fixture; original sequential update order retained. No biological or political inference.

title: One learning step
description: Sample the original loss function, expose its finite-difference gradient and learning rate, then follow source-computed steps.
limitation: A toy optimization surface, not a demonstration of neural-network learning or consciousness.

title: The graph keeps its connections
description: A source-generated tree spreads under repulsion and spring forces while its adjacency stays fixed.
limitation: A layout algorithm changes coordinates, not the meaning or validity of the graph.

title: Keep a connection; refuse a cycle
description: The seeded source graph is sorted by cost and original union-find joins components while rejecting cycles.
limitation: Arch height displays cost; a minimum spanning tree is not a shortest path.

title: A triangle depends on its surface
description: Source-generated straight and great-circle edges reveal different tangent angles on plane and sphere.
limitation: Separate geometric models; no continuous curvature interpolation, independent area theorem test, or Godel proof.

title: Same draws, a moving threshold
description: Lift fixed source-generated random draws into height, sweep the threshold, and distinguish sample count from binary source entropy.
limitation: Private 64-draw sample; H(p) is source entropy, not thermodynamic entropy or proof of QFEP.

title: No named root, unequal connections
description: Replay source growth with one or three earlier neighbours, then remove a high-degree node and its edges.
limitation: A source graph comparison, not evidence of social equality or an automatic interpretation of A Thousand Plateaus.
